transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-28
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Evan Ramirez, Maya Lin, Dale Foster, Rina Shah (Silverpoint)

Summary:
Quick console + API walkthrough focused on request storage modes, logging/redaction toggles, and PII scrubbing. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for a B2C retail personalization feature; main blockers are PCI/PII handling, audit trails, and retention policy enforcement. Demo shows console toggles, API flags, and sample beachhead PoC options.

Topics covered:
- Request storage: ephemeral vs stored (console toggle and per-request header)
- Redaction rules: regex-based, NER-based, and custom scrubbing pipelines
- Telemetry & audit logs: retention, user-level tracing, and export to SIEM
- KMS integration and key rotation for persisted request storage
- Sandbox PoC setup and success criteria

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: okay welcome everyone, thanks for carving out the time. quick intro — im Jordan, im the AE on this account, with Priya who will walk through the console and the API demos. Evan, Maya, thanks for joining.
[00:12] Evan: hey thanks jordan, we got a few people on from infra and security, we're mainly trying to understand how we can keep PII out of logs and still get enough telemetry for debugging.
[00:22] Jordan: totally. Priya, want to kick off the demo and show the two levers we usually talk about?
[00:27] Priya: yep, I'll share screen. so first thing — console home, under Project -> Data Controls. you can see Request Storage mode, default is "ephemeral" for new projects, but you can switch to "persisted" and then configure retention and encryption.
[00:40] Priya: note there are two places to control this: project-level toggle, and an API header for per-request override. so devs can send short lived requests for sensitive flows. that per-request header is x-redwood-request-storage with values ephemeral|persisted.
[00:56] Dale: sorry, per-request override is authenticated? like only certain service tokens can call persisted?
[00:59] Priya: good question — yes, RBAC. only tokens with the storage:write scope (or an allowed role) can set persisted. otherwise the project default is enforced.
[01:12] Maya: and what about scrubbers — we have credit-card numbers and emails in customer notes. how deterministic is the redaction?
[01:18] Priya: we have layered redaction. first pass is heuristic regex rules for common tokens (SSN, PAN, emails). second pass is NER-based detection tuned for names, addresses. and third is a custom pipeline — customers can upload regexes or a small script that runs in the pipeline (sandboxed) to mask vendor-specific tokens.
[01:38] Jordan: an important point — redaction occurs before any persisted log write. so if request is set to persisted but a PII token is detected, the saved copy has those tokens masked.
[01:49] Evan: what about false positives — will it mangle order IDs or SKU codes? we need to be careful.
[01:54] Priya: we provide a preview mode in the console. when you add a custom rule you can run the rule against a sample dataset and see matches/highlighted tokens. that preview doesn't store the sample unless you explicitly save it.
[02:07] Rina: can rules be versioned? we have a change control process.
[02:10] Priya: yes, rule sets are versioned. there's an audit trail, and each change can be annotated with rationale/PR link. the audit log shows who changed it and when.
[02:20] [02:21] Jordan: let's switch to the API flow — Priya can show a curl of a request with ephemeral vs persisted.
[02:26] Priya: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
        -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" 
        -H "x-redwood-request-storage: ephemeral" 
        -d '{ "prompt": "customer asks for order status #OID-12345 with cc 4111-1111-1111-1111" }'
[02:45] Priya: in ephemeral mode we will not write the raw request to disk, the KV cache is transient in memory. logs show request ID and token counts, but not the payload.
[02:54] Maya: do ephemeral requests still hit trace logs for latency debugging?
[02:58] Priya: yes, we emit telemetry events (latency, model used, token counts) without including the request text. full traces are anonymized. if you want to debug and see the payload you need persisted mode and appropriate RBAC.
[03:12] Dale: okay if we set persisted but rely on redaction, what's our guarantee? do you keep original for a given retention window?
[03:20] Priya: persisted stores the redacted version only. we never keep an unredacted original in the default flow. there is an optional escrow mode for customers that require original for legal reasons, but that requires enterprise contract and HSM-backed KMS with split keys.
[03:36] Evan: escrow mode — can you explain? our legal said they might need raw for 30 days in rare disputes.
[03:41] Jordan: escrow is rare but exists. it's off by default. if a customer elects escrow, we store the original encrypted with a customer-managed key and Redwood's key in a dual-KMS pattern; access requires documented approvals and audit trail. that's typically only for sensitive legal holds.
[03:58] Maya: encryption — how does KMS integration look? rotate keys? satisfy key rotation policies?
[04:03] Priya: we support both Redwood-managed KMS and bring-your-own-key (BYOK). for BYOK you can supply a cloud KMS key (AWS/GCP/Azure) or use an HSM + KMS connector. key rotation is supported; when you rotate a key we rewrap metadata pointers but encrypted blobs remain unreadable without the previous key for the remainder of retention unless you enable key rotation re-encryption.
[04:24] [04:25] Rina: SLA / latency hit for persisted with redaction — is there measurable penalty?
[04:30] Priya: minimal for most flows. redaction runs as a lightweight pass; if you enable heavy custom pipelines there can be added CPU latency. we also offer asynchronous persistence: synchronous response returns quickly, and persistence + indexing runs in a background job. you can choose sync vs async per project.
[04:46] Evan: any constraints for PCI workloads? we process tokenized PANs today but cannot store raw PANs. can Redwood certify?
[04:56] Jordan: Redwood isn't a PCI processor by default. we can support PCI patterns if customers use tokenization and ensure raw PAN never leaves their environment. for on-prem or private deployments we have patterns that can meet PCI with additional controls; we'd want to scope offline to see if it fits your audit.
[05:10] Maya: audit log export — we want to ship logs to Splunk/Datadog. retention there is different but we need the logs to show redaction events and who changed rules.
[05:18] Priya: export works via the Audit Export job or streaming connector. exports include metadata: rule-id, mask-hash, user, timestamp. we avoid exporting raw payloads unless configured.
[05:27] [05:30] Jordan: quick demo of the rule preview: adding a regex for internal SKU pattern, run preview -> shows 18 matches, you can mark false positives and add an exclusion list.
[05:44] Dale: nice — we can use that to avoid masking SKU-#### patterns.
[05:47] [06:00] Priya: now i want to show Optimize recommendations — console -> Optimize -> Cost & Latency. for request storage heavy flows we recommend batching + prefix caching to reduce repeated sensitive tokens being sent. Optimize suggests turning on prefix cache for support workflows, and shows estimated cost delta if you persist vs ephemeral.
[06:20] Evan: can Optimize tie into our telemetry to recommend quantization or smaller model family for certain flows?
[06:26] Priya: yes, Optimize connects to token-level traces and makes model recommendations. it will flag privacy-sensitive flows and recommend ephemeral defaults and smaller models for bulk processing.
[06:36] Rina: is there an API for Optimize so we can run analysis programmatically?
[06:39] Priya: yes there's a /v1/optimize/export endpoint that returns recommended config edits as JSON.
[06:47] [07:00] Speaker 6: (inaudible)
[07:05] Maya: what's the granularity for retention — can we set retention per-route?
[07:09] Priya: yes — project, route, or per-request header. retention is expressed as days/weeks/months and we support custom TTL policies. you can also set a policy that auto-ejects requests matching a pattern (e.g., if subject contains "ssn" then TTL = 0).
[07:25] Jordan: ejection — that's important. ejection means the system never persists the request beyond ephemeral memory. it can also trigger a notification to your security queue when a match occurs.
[07:36] Evan: how do we handle chain-of-responsibility in rollouts? if we adjust rules during a canary, will older persisted logs be re-scrubbed?
[07:44] Priya: re-scrubbing is off by default; you can opt into a re-scrub job that will reprocess historical persisted records with a new rule set. we keep a snapshot to allow rollbacks in case of over-scrubbing. re-scrub jobs are auditable and show diff counts.
[07:59] Dale: sounds good. any limits on retention windows?
[08:03] Priya: default max is 3650 days (10 years) for enterprise; hosted accounts have a soft limit 5 years but we can extend. there are cost implications obviously.
[08:14] [08:15] Jordan: let's go through a quick scenario — Rina, you mentioned the personalization flow where engineers sometimes log the raw user prompt. how would you set this up?
[08:23] Rina: yes, personalization service calls Redwood to generate recommendations using PII. we want ephemeral by default and persisted only for debugging with approvals.
[08:30] Priya: recommended setup: project default = ephemeral, create a debug route where persisted is allowed but scoped to a role. add a rule set that masks email/phone, enable rule preview, and set retention for persisted debug data to 30 days. also wire Audit Export to your SIEM for change events.
[08:49] Evan: can we automate approvals? we have a microservice that could call an approvals API.
[08:53] Priya: yes, we have a programmatic approvals endpoint — approvals are recorded as policy exceptions with TTL and reason.
[08:59] Maya: another question — will function/tool-calling or plugins leak anything in logs?
[09:04] Priya: function-call payloads are treated like any other request. we offer additional scrubbing for tool outputs because they often include 3rd-party URIs; you can configure allow-lists and dynamic masking.
[09:15] [09:30] Jordan: we're about halfway, want to pause for any security deep-dive or should we continue the sandbox demo?
[09:36] Maya: let's dig into encryption details for persisted storage for 10 mins.
[09:40] Priya: sure — data at rest uses envelope encryption: per-blob data key encrypted with KMS key. for BYOK the customer KMS wraps the data key — Redwood does not hold the customer plaintext KMS key. HSM integration available for Private deployments.
[09:58] Evan: key escrow and legal holds — if we need to produce raw data for a subpoena, what's Redwood's process?
[10:06] Jordan: typically you'd request an export; if escrow was not enabled we can only export redacted data. if you anticipate legal holds you must enable escrow and the dual-key pattern up front. retrieval requires multi-party approval and logs are given to you as part of the procedure.
[10:22] Rina: what's the change window for rule changes in prod? our compliance requires 48hr notice.
[10:26] Priya: you can require a staged rollout policy: new rules go to canary for 24h, then to staged, then to prod, and the system can enforce a minimum review time before promotion.
[10:39] [10:45] Jordan: i'm going to show the sandbox we pre-provisioned — Priya, switch to sample data.
[10:50] Priya: here's the sample: 'Order 8349, email maya@example.com, card 4111-1111-1111-1111'. project default ephemeral — console call shows no persisted entry. switch request to persisted by setting header and you see a redacted entry in the request store: 'Order 8349, email [EMAIL_REDACTED], card [PAN_REDACTED]'.
[11:10] Dale: where do the redaction tokens map to — do we store hash or fixed token?
[11:14] Priya: we store a salted hash mapping so you can correlate the same entity across requests without exposing the value. mapping can be scoped to project or global; salted per-project by default.
[11:26] Evan: correlation is useful for dedup and fraud detection — can we export the mapping table?
[11:31] Priya: you can export hashed tokens but not the original. export includes salt metadata so it can only be used by your account.
[11:40] Rina: we'll need that for linking events.
[11:45] [11:58] Jordan: quick break — any outstanding architecture concerns?
[12:02] Evan: want to confirm on prem/private deploy differences — are toggles and redaction pipelines the same?
[12:08] Priya: yes, feature parity for Private but the KMS connectors and audit integrations depend on your environment. some managed connectors (like our Splunk streaming) need network egress; private installs can wire them directly to your SIEM.
[12:22] Maya: and concurrency/throughput on private — if we run heavy redaction pipelines will you recommend dedicated GPUs?
[12:28] Priya: redaction is CPU-bound pre-processing typically; model inference is GPU-bound. for heavy rule processing we recommend dedicated CPU pools for preprocessing, then model pools for inference. Redwood Dedicated supports configuring separate pools.
[12:46] [13:00] Jordan: wrapping up the demo, quick recap and suggested PoC plan.
[13:06] Priya: propose 4-week PoC: week 1 sandbox + sample ingest; week 2 run ingestion with ephemeral defaults and test redaction accuracy; week 3 run persisted + re-scrub simulations; week 4 integrate audit export and measure cost impact.
[13:20] Jordan: success criteria — 95% redaction accuracy on PII categories, no raw PAN stored, SIEM audit export working, and a perf profile showing <250ms added p50 latency for sync flows or acceptable async persistence.
[13:36] Evan: sounds reasonable. on cost we will need ballpark numbers for persisted at scale.
[13:40] Jordan: i'll include cost estimates in the follow-up. Priya will spin up the sandbox credentials.
[13:47] Maya: i'm going to send our data classification spreadsheet as promised.
[13:51] Rina: and we'll identify the team for the PoC.
[13:55] Jordan: great — thanks everyone. final quick notes: I'll mail SOC2 and encryption note; Priya will post sandbox link and sample API curl; we'll schedule PoC scoping with your infra and security.
[14:10] Evan: thanks all, that was helpful.
[14:14] Jordan: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.

Notes about quality and caveats: Transcript contains a few misheard words and a couple of brief inaudible segments; speaker labels were mostly accurate though one attendee appeared as "Speaker 6" due to the conferencing tool. The demo included code snippets as shown and console screenshots referenced but not captured in this export.
